benchmark.name: Sequential SfM vs COLMAP head-to-head (metric video)
benchmark.protocol: Same rectified EuRoC MH_03_medium 2700-frame stereo image stream reconstructed by both engines and scored against the same timestamped Vicon/Leica ground truth with the same evo_ape tooling (DROID/DPVO same-tool battle pattern). COLMAP arm: monocular sequential_matcher + incremental mapper (its SIFT frontend), scale-free, so its trajectory needs a Sim(3) (scale-fitted) alignment to the metric ground truth.

command.raw: scripts/run_sfm_vs_colmap_battle.sh --rect-dir /tmp/MH_03_rect --feat-dir /tmp/sp_MH_03 --gt /tmp/MH_03_gt.tum --frames 2700 --out-dir target/sfm_vs_colmap  # documented prior invocation; COLMAP mapper stage alone took ~11.5h, full run 11.7h -- NOT re-run in this session

params.mapper: incremental mapper (global BA interleaved per registration)

dataset.name: EuRoC MAV
dataset.version: ASL EuRoC MAV dataset, full 2700 frames

hardware.notes: Single CPU machine; COLMAP 4.0.3 built/run without CUDA.

metrics.implementation: COLMAP 4.0.3 sequential_matcher + incremental mapper, no CUDA (mapper stage alone ~11.5h of the 11.7h total)
metrics.name: wall_clock

metrics.implementation: evo_ape, Sim(3) (scale-absorbed) alignment against Vicon/Leica ground truth; monocular reconstruction is scale-free so Sim(3) alignment is required
metrics.name: ate_sim3

notes: PRIOR-RUN reference, NOT reproduced in this session. COLMAP 4.0.3, no CUDA, single CPU machine, per docs/sfm_vs_colmap_benchmark.md. The documented wall-clock cost (11.7h total, mapper stage alone ~11.5h, reaching only ~310/2700 frames after 31 minutes because the incremental mapper's interleaved global BA is super-linear in registered-image count) makes a local re-run impractical for this evidence-formalization pass; COLMAP is also not installed on this machine. This manifest therefore captures the already-documented, previously-executed COLMAP result as registry evidence rather than re-executing it. build.cargo_lock_sha256/rustc/cargo are null because this run does not exercise the visloc-rs Rust build at all (COLMAP is an external tool); result_kind=external_rerun and claim_scope=supporting reflect that this is a comparison reference, not a visloc-rs claim in its own right. downstream_3dgs="blurry" is the same fly-through capture-geometry limit as the visloc arm -- identical for both engines on this forward-flight sequence, not a pose-quality difference between them. Honest scope note: this MH_03 metric-video result is NOT a claim that visloc-rs beats COLMAP on COLMAP's unordered-photo home turf -- on the 300-frame monocular subset (both engines monocular, scored the same way) COLMAP wins, 0.37cm vs visloc 1.64cm; see docs/sfm_vs_colmap_benchmark.md and docs/generated/sfm_vs_colmap_headtohead.md for that comparison.
